scope: Research-only record of national crop production estimates, agricultural structure, cocoa-sector signals, food-import dependence, macroeconomic and source-quality context. This is not a farm-profit calculator profile and does not authorize country activation.

currency.name: Central African CFA franc
currency.note: Currency identification only. No verified, dated farm-gate crop prices or farm input quotations have been added.

context.agroecology: Humid equatorial environment with mainland and island production zones. The FAO identifies cassava, sweet potatoes, plantains, groundnuts and bananas among staple crops, with cocoa a leading cash crop. Country-level figures should not be assumed to represent all provinces or Bioko and Río Muni equally.
context.caution: The available public sources provide useful national production and policy context but not a complete, reconciled crop-area/yield dataset or commercial farm budgets. Distinguish FAOSTAT estimates from national survey/administrative observations, and distinguish imported consumer-market food from local producer prices.

administrative_geography.source_note: The 2026 UK Permanent Committee on Geographical Names official Toponymic Factfile identifies two regions and eight first-order provinces. The 2026 INEGE yearbook confirms that selected statistics are disaggregated by region, province and district. Districts must not be mixed into the province selector.

observations_text: FAO states that weather conditions during the 2026 growing season had generally been favourable and forecasts sweet potato, cassava and plantain production near average levels in 2026.
The reported 2024 crop quantities are production totals, not yields; harvested area by crop is required before deriving tonnes per hectare.
evidence.caveat: The 850,000-hectare arable-land figure and the approximate 20,000-hectare staple plus 9,000-hectare cash-crop cultivated areas are distinct concepts and should not be added or treated as a complete land-use balance. FAO's June 2025 country brief gave materially different land-use figures (about 280,000 ha agricultural land, with 180,000 ha used for staple crops). This discrepancy requires reconciliation against the underlying FAOSTAT series and national land-use definitions before operational use.

evidence.topic: Agricultural productivity comparison and input policy
evidence.source: International Monetary Fund, Republic of Equatorial Guinea: Selected Issues / Country Report No. 24/25
observations_text: The IMF reports that FAO 2021 yield data for cassava, plantains and bananas were as much as three to four times higher in neighbouring Cameroon than in Equatorial Guinea; it also identifies similar productivity gaps for cocoa and palm oil.
The IMF identifies agriculture and fisheries as potential employment and diversification sectors and points to improved seed varieties and fertilizer use as potential productivity measures.
evidence.caveat: This is a comparative productivity finding based on 2021 FAO data, not a current national yield table. The accessible source summary does not supply the exact crop-by-crop yields, units or harvested-area denominators. Do not use the Cameroon comparison as a yield target or as a calculator input.

evidence.source: FAO GIEWS, Equatorial Guinea Country Brief

observations.indicator: Domestic food needs covered by commercial imports

observations.source_note: IMF estimate quoted by FAO; forecast/estimate in the country brief.

evidence.caveat: Import volumes and food import dependence describe national food supply and trade, not local farm-gate demand or producer prices. Wheat and rice import forecasts must not be treated as domestic production.

evidence.topic: World Bank economic and diversification context
evidence.source: World Bank, Equatorial Guinea Economic Update 2025: Managing Equatorial Guinea's Wealth for Sustainable Growth and Development
observations_text: The World Bank describes the need to diversify the economy and identifies an integrated approach involving land-use planning, sustainable agriculture, clean energy and ecotourism.
The update reports that food-price pressures and limited employment opportunities have contributed to poverty and weak living standards.
evidence.caveat: This is macroeconomic and policy context, not a crop production dataset, producer-price source or farm enterprise budget.

evidence.source: International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), Equatorial Guinea country page
observations_text: IFAD lists a Climate Resilient Agrifood Value Chains Development Project with a stated cost of US$42.66 million and identifies earlier agricultural development and crop-diversification projects.
IFAD lists a 2025-2027 Country Strategy Note.
evidence.caveat: Programme budgets and project listings are not proof of disbursement, farm-level reach, crop output or realised producer benefits. Project documents and monitoring results should be checked before recording beneficiary counts or production impacts.

evidence.source: FAOSTAT, Crops and livestock products dataset
observations_text: FAOSTAT is the primary international dataset identified by FAO GIEWS for the 2023 and 2024 national crop production estimates cited above.
Country-level extraction is still required for crop-specific harvested area, production, yield, livestock inventories and products, including observation flags and estimation status.
evidence.caveat: No raw FAOSTAT country export has yet been attached to this record. Until extracted, retain FAO GIEWS-reported aggregates as secondary transcriptions and do not present them as independently revalidated raw FAOSTAT rows.

evidence.topic: INEGE Statistical Yearbook 2026 and current administrative geography
evidence.source: INEGE, Statistical Yearbook of Equatorial Guinea 2026; UK Permanent Committee on Geographical Names, Equatorial Guinea Toponymic Factfile (2026)
observations_text: INEGE released the 2026 Statistical Yearbook on 25 September 2026; the publication compiles official statistics updated through December 2025 and covers agriculture, prices, wages, and other sectors.
INEGE states that selected yearbook statistics are disaggregated by region, province and district, but the crop tables and numeric observations still need to be extracted and checked.
INEGE's release summary reports cocoa production grew 2.5% in the 2024/2025 agricultural season; this is a growth rate, not a production tonnage, crop yield or farmgate price.

The 2026 official toponymic factfile identifies two regions (Continental and Insular) and eight first-order provinces: Annobón, Bioko Norte, Bioko Sur, Centro Sur, Djibloho, Kié-Ntem, Litoral and Wele-Nzas.
evidence.caveat: The yearbook landing page and release summary do not themselves provide extracted crop-area, production, yield, farmgate price or farm-input tables. Do not convert the cocoa growth rate into an absolute output value or use it as a producer price. Province list is suitable for a first-level selector; province-specific crop data and boundary crosswalks remain unverified.

data_quality_and_use: The strongest recent crop evidence is FAO's July 2026 publication of 2024 FAOSTAT production estimates for sweet potatoes, cassava and plantains.

INEGE's September 2026 Statistical Yearbook is the priority national source for crop, price and regional tables; the public announcement confirms scope and cocoa growth but does not expose detailed tables in its accessible text.

FAO's June 2025 and July 2026 briefs report materially different agricultural/arable land and staple-crop area figures. Preserve both with dates and definitions and resolve the discrepancy before using land or yield calculations.
The 2024/2025 cocoa growth figure is a percentage change only; no absolute output or farmgate price is supplied in the public INEGE summary.
The IMF's 2021 comparative yield finding signals productivity constraints but does not supply usable current crop-level yield values in the accessible extract.
Food import dependence is high; import volumes and consumer food inflation are not substitutes for local producer price series.
No verified current farm-gate prices, input prices, labour costs, crop-specific enterprise budgets or regional market margins have been established in this review.

The 2026 INEGE yearbook is a current official source inventory, but no crop-level numeric tables have yet been extracted from it. Its reported 2.5% cocoa production growth for 2024/2025 is not a crop tonnage, yield or farmgate price.
missing_data_before_calculator_use: Download and extract the agriculture and price tables from the complete INEGE Statistical Yearbook 2026, including table titles, units, reference years, methodology, source department and any province/district breakdown.
Reconcile FAO's 2025 and 2026 agricultural land and staple-crop area estimates against INEGE/FAOSTAT definitions and raw data.

Extract FAOSTAT 2024 country rows for cassava, sweet potatoes, plantains, bananas, groundnuts, cocoa, palm products and other priority crops, including harvested area, production, yield, flags and notes.

Obtain crop-specific farm-gate prices by province/market, date, grade and unit, especially cassava, plantain, sweet potato, banana, cocoa and groundnut; distinguish farm-gate, wholesale and retail prices.
Obtain current input quotations for seed/planting material, fertilizer, crop protection, hired labour, land preparation, tools/equipment, irrigation, transport, packaging and storage.
Obtain representative farm budgets and crop calendars by agroecological zone and production system, with marketable yield, crop losses, labour requirements and financing costs.
Obtain current cocoa procurement prices, quality/grade deductions, producer organisation and buyer-channel information, and season-specific costs.
Obtain livestock and fisheries census/production statistics, animal prices, feed and veterinary costs, and value-chain margins if those enterprises are to be included.
Validate IFAD project implementation and monitoring data before using programme targets or planned investment as evidence of realised production or farmer income.
Extract and validate the agriculture tables in the 2026 INEGE yearbook, including commodity, area, production, yield, year/season, geography, units and source agency; reconcile with FAOSTAT.
recommendation: Keep Equatorial Guinea research-only. Add the verified eight-province first-level selector for future regional data entry, but do not activate a calculator profile until crop-level tables, dated farmgate prices, input quotations, labour/machinery/irrigation costs, regional enterprise budgets, currency handling, schema mapping and test cases are validated.
